context.title: Everyone Builds a Section
context.summary: The chapter records who rebuilt each section of the wall and each gate, going around the city. Priests, rulers, goldsmiths, perfumers, merchants and ordinary families all take part.
context.background: The list moves counterclockwise from the Sheep Gate near the temple. Many repaired the wall nearest their own homes (vv. 10, 23, 28–30). Shallum worked with his daughters (v. 12), while the nobles of Tekoa refused to work, though the Tekoites did two sections (vv. 5, 27).

customs.term: Put not their necks to the work
customs.note: An image from the ox's yoke — they refused to bear the burden of labor.
A gate near the temple, likely where sacrificial animals were brought in.

watchFor: The high priest is the first to build (v. 1).
The repeated phrase 'next unto him' ties the whole effort together.

people.name: Meremoth
people.summary: Exaltations, heights, a priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:3), to whom were sent the sacred vessels (Ezra 8:33) belonging to the temple.

people.name: Berechiah
people.summary: The father of Meshullam the builder.

people.name: Urijah
people.summary: The father of Meremoth, mentioned in Ezra 8:33.

people.name: Meshezabeel
people.summary: Ancestor of Meshullam, who assisted Nehemiah in rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem.

people.name: Zadok
people.summary: The sons of Baana, one of those who assisted in rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:4).

people.name: Jadon
people.summary: Judge, a Meronothite who assisted in rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:7).

people.name: Harhaiah
people.summary: Zeal of Jehovah, (Neh. 3:8) “of the goldsmiths,” one whose son helped to repair the wall of Jerusalem.

people.name: Rephaiah
people.summary: Ruler of a half-district of Jerusalem.

people.name: Jedaiah
people.summary: One of those who repaired the walls of Jerusalem after the return from Babylon (Neh. 3:10).

people.name: Shallum
people.summary: Ruler of a district of Jerusalem.

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Zabbai
people.summary: The father of Baruch, who “earnestly repaired” part of the wall of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:20; marg., “Zaccai”).

people.name: Parosh
people.summary: The ancestor of one of the families which returned to Jerusalem from captivity in Babylon.

people.name: Shechaniah
people.summary: The father of Shemaiah, who repaired the wall of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:29).

places.name: sheep gate
places.summary: One of the gates of Jerusalem mentioned by Nehemiah (3:1, 32; 12:39).

places.name: Tower
places.summary: God has graciously given, a tower in the wall of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:1; 12:39).

places.name: Jericho
places.summary: Place of fragrance, a fenced city in the midst of a vast grove of palm trees, in the plain of Jordan, over against the place where that river was crossed by the Israelites (Josh. 3:16).

places.name: fish gate
places.summary: Of cities, as of Jerusalem (Jer. 37:13; Neh. 1:3; 2:3; 3:3), of Sodom (Gen. 19:1), of Gaza (Judg. 16:3).

places.name: old gate
places.summary: One of the gates in the north wall of Jerusalem, so called because built by the Jebusites (Neh. 3:6; 12:39).

places.name: Gibeon
places.summary: Hill-city, “one of the royal cities, greater than Ai, and all the men thereof were mighty” (Josh. 10:2). Its inhabitants were Hivites (11:19).

places.name: Mizpah
places.summary: A city of Benjamin, “the watch-tower”, where the people were accustomed to meet in great national emergencies (Josh. 18:26; Judg. 20:1, 3; 21:1, 5; 1 Sam. 7:5-16).

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Tower
places.summary: (Neh. 3:11; 12:38), a tower at the north-western angle of the second wall of Jerusalem.

places.name: dung gate
places.summary: (Neh. 2:13), a gate of ancient Jerusalem, on the south-west quarter.

places.name: Zanoah
places.summary: A town in the low country or shephelah of Judah, near Zorah (Josh. 15:34). It was re-occupied after the return from the Captivity (Neh. 11:30).

places.name: Beth-haccherem
places.summary: House of a vineyard, a place in the tribe of Judah (Neh. 3:14) where the Benjamites were to set up a beacon when they heard the trumpet against the invading army of the Babylonians (Jer. 6:1).

places.name: Pool
places.summary: Heb. shelah; i.e., “the dart”, Neh. 3:15; with the art. shiloah, “sending,” Isa. 8:6 (comp. 7:3)=Siloam

places.name: Keilah
places.summary: Citadel, a city in the lowlands of Judah (Josh. 15:44). David rescued it from the attack of the Philistines (1 Sam. 23:1-8); but the inhabitants proving unfaithful to him, in that they sought to deliver him up to Saul (13), he and his men “departed from Keilah, and went whithersoever they could go.”

places.name: Ophel
places.summary: Hill; mound, the long, narrow, rounded promontory on the southern slope of the temple hill, between the Tyropoeon and the Kedron valley (2 Chr. 27:3; 33:14; Neh. 3:26, 27).

places.name: water gate
places.summary: The fruit of a species of palm, the Phoenix dactilifera. This was a common tree in Palestine (Joel 1:12; Neh. 8:15).

places.name: horse gate
places.summary: A gate in the wall of Jerusalem, at the west end of the bridge, leading from Zion to the temple (Neh. 3:28; Jer. 31:40).
